>>266666390
>still, I wouldn't give two thoughts about the masses.
>they are unreliable. work towards achieving our goal, the destruction of industrial society, and the masses WILL wake up at that moment. until then they are useless. 
You are correct, just like the rest of your post. But he also speaks of the importance of the basic ideas being made available, so when the time of 'disillusion' comes, the anti-tech idea is one of the possible answers. 
Think of cryptocoins as an example: very vry few people know what crypto is, much les how it works, but MANY people have heard the word 'Bitcoin', and the all know that it is 'electronic non-dollar money', so to speak. 
Disseminating Ted's ideas is worth the trouble. 

In any case, here are the quotes:
(page 111)
''First, while ideas by themselves will not transform a society, the development and propagation of ideas must be a part of any rational effort to transform a society. Without some organized set ofideas to guide its action, a movement will flounder aimlessly. It may generate more or less uproar, but if it accomplishes anything more than that it will do so merely through luck.''
(page 168)
''Seldom indeed will you succeed in persuading your opponents in an
ideological dispute. Therefore, in any such dispute, your arguments should
be designed not to persuade your opponents but to influence undecided
third parties who may hear or read the arguments. For this purpose you
should state your case concisely, as clearly and convincingly as possible, and in a way that will make it interesting to third parties. Then do what you can to ensure that your arguments are widely heard or read.

Obviously, it is this very last sentence that is the most important regarding the dissemination of ideas.'' 

>I don't think Ellul's book has been translated.
That sucks.
